news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire's climate emissions cuts fall 69% as LED streetlighting plan loses funding
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's Environment and Infrastructure Services Committee has scaled back its planned carbon reductions for 2026/27 from 81 tonnes to 25 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, after capital funding for LED streetlighting was not allocated. In its Carbon Budget progress update, the council identified the streetlighting rollout as the main project now unable to proceed. The committee acknowledged that meeting its climate change targets requires "significant capital investment" for which long-term funding has not yet been secured. Budget pressures, the council stated, can only be managed if additional funding becomes available to support the capital spending needed for those targets.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire IJB returns to surplus but remains dependent on partner funding
news_drafts.lead: The Aberdeenshire Integration Joint Board has closed a year-end surplus and created a small general fund reserve for the first time in the accounts to 31 March 2026, marking a marked improvement on the previous year through recovery activity, partner support and strengthened financial controls. The committee noted this was the beginning of a longer-term improvement rather than a final position. Officers confirmed that reserves available in the current financial year remained limited and the IJB continued to rely on partner funding to deliver a balanced budget while savings plans were implemented. External audit has identified medium-term financial sustainability as a key focus, reflecting structural challenges including demand pressures, workforce capacity constraints and the need for service redesign. The chief internal auditor provided the most positive opinion available under internal audit standards, confirming the IJB maintained an adequate and effective framework for governance, risk management and control during the year.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire health and social care partnership achieves £19m savings but five key performance measures fall below Scottish average
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's health and social care partnership delivered £19 million of savings in 2025/26, about 70% of them recurring, and moved from years of chronic overspend to a break-even position. The shift came through strengthened financial management and a planned savings and transformation programme. However, the partnership's performance on five National Indicators of care quality has declined between 2023/24 and 2025/26, all now more than 5% below the Scottish average: the proportion of people able to live independently fell from 73.6% to 67.8%; those having a say in their care from 63.9% to 55.9%; GP experience from 70.7% to 62.2%; and people feeling safe from 74.7% to 69.4%. Hospital delayed discharge also worsened, rising from 687 to 818 days per 1,000 population aged 75 and over in a single year. The partnership's budget covers £485 million in annual spending.

findings.headline: Total reserves forecast at £21,539k at 30 September 2026, from a revised opening balance of £20,992k at 1 April 2026
findings.detail: The total of all reserves shows a revised opening balance of £20,992k, a current balance of £20,479k, and a forecast of £21,539k at 30 September 2026. The forecast rise over the current balance is driven by the £1,450k transfer to the Affordable Housing Reserve within the HRA earmarked reserves, which are forecast at £14,204k.
findings.matters: Total reserves rising while General Fund reserves fall shows the mix shifting toward ring-fenced HRA and housing balances, which a finance director comparing reserve composition across councils would note.
findings.figures: Revised opening balance £20,992k; current balance £20,479k; forecast at 30 Sep 2026 £21,539k; HRA earmarked reserves forecast £14,204k

findings.headline: General Fund Earmarked Reserves forecast at £7,335k at 30 September 2026, from £8,228k at 1 April 2026
findings.detail: The General Fund earmarked reserves show a revised opening balance of £8,228k, a current balance of £7,725k, and a forecast of £7,335k at 30 September 2026. The paper notes that all figures are provisional pending finalisation of the 2025/26 outturn.
findings.matters: A general fund reserve falling across the year, with the figures still subject to outturn, is a position a finance director would track against the council's own reserves strategy and peers' general fund balances.
findings.figures: Opening balance £8,228k; current balance £7,725k; forecast at 30 Sep 2026 £7,335k; transfer from reserves £519k

findings.headline: Earmarked reserve for government grants forecast at £6,560k at 30 September 2026, down from £7,401k at 1 April 2026, with £467k transferred out so far
findings.detail: The grant-funded reserves show a revised opening balance of £7,401k, a transfer from reserves of £467k, and a current balance of £6,950k. The largest single line, Refugee Resettlement Funding, moves from £5,926k to £5,567k after a £359k transfer from reserves. The paper states these reserves have legal or funding restrictions on their use.
findings.matters: Grant reserves drawn down against conditions show how quickly restricted government funding is being spent, which finance officers at other councils managing refugee and asylum funding would compare directly.
findings.figures: Opening balance £7,401k; transfer from reserves £467k; current balance £6,950k; forecast at 30 Sep 2026 £6,560k; Refugee Resettlement Funding £5,926k opening, £359k transferred, £5,567k current

findings.headline: Affordable Housing Reserve forecast at £13,404k at 30 September 2026, up from a current balance of £11,954k, after a £1,450k transfer to reserves
findings.detail: The paper shows the Affordable Housing Reserve with a current balance of £11,954k and a transfer to reserves of £1,450k, giving a forecast of £13,404k at 30 September 2026. The reserve is funded from council tax on second homes and long-term empty properties, which Scottish Government legislation requires to be used for affordable housing.
findings.matters: A reserve funded by a statutory council tax share and held until projects are identified is a restricted balance whose forecast growth shows how much housing funding is being held back rather than spent, which a finance director or lender would compare with peer councils' housing reserves.
findings.figures: Current balance £11,954k; transfer to reserves £1,450k; forecast balance at 30 Sep 2026 £13,404k; paper shows reserve balances in brackets

findings.headline: The council recorded 178 new supply affordable housing completions in 2025/26, against 180 in 2024/25 and 259 in 2023/24
findings.detail: The 2023/24 figure excludes 51 Create Homes units. The paper reports 159 social rent completions in 2025/26, of which 73 came from the Council New Build programme and 86 from RSL partners.
findings.matters: Completion volumes against a stated housing supply target of 250 units a year show the delivery pace other councils will be measured against.
findings.figures: 178 completions (2025/26); 180 (2024/25); 259 (2023/24); 159 social rent (2025/26); 250 units a year (affordable supply target)
